newsitem.title: NORWAY: Leif Hoegh finalises reefer group deal.
newsitem.headline: Leif Hoegh finalises reefer group deal.

text.p: Norwegian shipowner Leif Hoegh & Co ASA said on Wednesday it had finalised an agreement to merge its refrigerated ship operations with those of Safmarine of South Africa to form the world's largest specialised reefer group.

Leif Hoegh added that it had also acquired the reefer interest in the new company originally intended to be held by Tufton Oceanic and the British company's stake in Cool Carriers AB of Sweden for a total $16.2 million. Cool Carriers was a joint venture between Leif Hoegh and Tufton Oceanic, which held a 25 percent interest.

Leif Hoegh said in a statement to the Oslo Stock Exchange that the new company, Unicool Ltd, would be 50-percent owned by Safmarine, 49.8 percent by Leif Hoegh and 0.2 percent by Mats Jansson, Unicool's managing director.
The agreement to form Unicool was announced in December but legal technicalities have taken time to complete.
UniCool controls a fleet of about 85 vessels, including 18 wholly-owned, with a total capacity of 36 million cubic feet, or 28 percent of all operator-controlled reefer tonnage, Leif Hoegh said.
Total assets of the new company, which is based on Bermuda, are now valued at around $400 million.
